## Why This Is Asked

Tests practical RBAC knowledge: namespace-scoped Roles, RoleBinding usage, and least-privilege design. It checks ability to translate a policy into concrete Kubernetes objects and validate permissions.

## Key Concepts

- RBAC basics: Role, RoleBinding, service accounts
- Namespace scoping vs ClusterRoles
- least privilege: read-only access for visibility, no write rights
- testing permissions with kubectl can-i

## Code Example

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ServiceAccount
metadata:
  name: dev-read
  namespace: dev
---
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: Role
metadata:
  name: pod-reader
  namespace: dev
rules:
- apiGroups: [""]
  resources: ["pods"]
  verbs: ["get", "list", "watch"]
---
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: RoleBinding
metadata:
  name: dev-read-binding
  namespace: dev
subjects:
- kind: ServiceAccount
  name: dev-read
  namespace: dev
roleRef:
  kind: Role
  name: pod-reader
  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you extend this to cover multiple namespaces while keeping separation?
- How would you audit and rotate these permissions across clusters?

## Why This Is Asked

```bash
kubectl get peerauthentication -n kcsa-prod
kubectl get authorizationpolicy -n kcsa-prod

# Reweight canary traffic gradually

apiVersion: networking.istio.io/v1alpha3
kind: VirtualService
metadata:
  name: my-app
  namespace: kcsa-prod
spec:
  http:
  - route:
    - destination:
        host: my-app.kcsa-prod.svc.cluster.local
        subset: canary

    - destination:
        host: my-app.kcsa-prod.svc.cluster.local

YAML
```

## Why This Is Asked

- Pod resource pressure and OOM considerations
- Istio Envoy proxy metrics and proxy-status insights

- Canary rollouts with zero downtime and rollback criteria
- Observability: tracing, metrics, and alarm thresholds

## Code Example
```bash
# Quick resource check
kubectl top pod -n kcsa-prod
# Identify a suspect pod
kubectl describe pod reco-api-abc123 -n kcsa-prod
# Envoy proxy status and stats
istioctl proxy-status -n kcsa-prod
kubectl exec <pod-name> -c istio-proxy -- curl http://localhost:15000/stats
# Redis performance analysis
redis-cli --latency-history
redis-cli INFO stats
# Cache key audit
redis-cli KEYS "*" | head -20
redis-cli GET <key>
# Canary deployment

# P95 latency monitoring
histogram_quantile(0.95, rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m]))
```
